- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.75), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is trending up.  
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon (e.g., days 1–5) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive — apply downward bias to first 5 days.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots — cap forecast at +3% above prior day’s high for next 3 days.  
- If sentiment turns sharply negative after a spike, model fails to correct — add a “mean reversion” rule: if 3-day average of sentiment < 0.3, reduce forecast by 1–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed or volatile — use sentiment median as a smoothing filter before forecasting.  
- If last 3 sentiment values are >0.5, forecast should be slightly above historical mean; if <0.3, slightly below.  
- Model often misses “reversal” patterns — if sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3 days, forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–2% per day for next 3 days.
